claims.summary: For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and F(i) = i^(3/4) + (2 + log_2 i) sqrt(log log N) (at most i^(3/4) + C (log log N)^(3/2)), with probability tending to one: (a) for every partition of [0,1]^2 into dyadic squares of sides 2^(-i), 1 <= i <= l_1 (the Leighton-Shor scale), and every H constant on its cells, |sum_i H(X_i) - N int H| <= L sqrt N sum over inner edges e of length(e) |jump_e H| F(i(e)), i(e) the level of the smaller cell beside e; (b) for every such partition in which neighbouring cells differ in side by a factor at most 2, and every Lipschitz G, |sum_i G(X_i) - N int G| <= L sqrt N sum_Q F(i(Q)) int_Q (|d_1 G| + |d_2 G|) + L sqrt(N log N) sum_Q Lip(G on Q) area(Q). In (b) G may be Lipschitz on each cell only, its jumps across edges added at their edges' factors.
claims.assessment: Working proof: telescoping H = H_1 + sum (H_k - H_(k-1)) over geometric levels j_k = 2^(k-1) on coarsened partitions; each difference vanishes off the refined blocks and is bounded by lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy with the deviation of lem:loglog-mesh-deviation; jumps controlled by a strip-trace inequality (sum of s_R |avg_R H - avg_B H| along a side of B at most |DH|(B), by a one-dimensional argument), the translation sweep, and their combination for unequal neighbours; each edge counted only at levels up to its own; (b) adds the cellwise remainder of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split.
claims.rationale: Charges every edge, or every cell's gradient mass, at its own scale's Leighton-Shor factor, so a class function can be split on a partition adapted to its gradient levels; by order estimates (constants not computed), the two-level case of the coarea mechanism for conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy then needs thickness of each level's support and a ring condition.
claims.next_action: Check whether the vertically scaled tents of lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound are thin bands beyond the mesh j*(y) and exceed the target there; then whether every class function at (4,4) splits into pieces satisfying the ring condition with costs adding up to a constant.
